Six things holding your website back

We read your website the way Google does. None of these is hard to fix, and none of them is about speed.

  • 1

    “Transform Your Space Now”, 11 times

    The homepage text a visitor (and Google) reads is that one line repeated eleven times by the slider, then the footer. There’s no sentence saying what you do or where.

  • 2

    No headline on any page

    None of the 12 pages we checked has a main heading, the first thing Google reads to understand a page.

  • 3

    Your Google description is form junk

    The summary Google can show under your link reads “…Send Your Enquiry Full Name Email Phone Number Select Service…”, text from your quote form.

  • 4

    “A global leader in landscaping”

    Leftover template copy in that description calls you a global leader. You’re a family business in the East Valley, which is a better story.

  • 5

    Only about 200 words on the homepage

    Pages that rank explain services, areas and what makes you different. Yours has a slider and a footer.

  • 6

    Portfolio photos Google can’t read

    45 of the 49 images on your portfolio page have no description, so your best work is invisible to search.

You already win on social

3K Instagram followers and a Google post every week. Most landscapers never do that. The website is the only piece lagging.

Say who you are in one line

“Family-owned landscape maintenance for Mesa, Gilbert and the East Valley, since 2018” instead of a repeated slogan.

Fix what Google shows

A clean description and headings on every page, so search shows a real summary instead of form fields.

Put the portfolio to work

Describe each portfolio photo (“front yard refresh, Gilbert”) so your projects show up in image search.

Same crew, every visit. 🌿 Family-owned since 2018, 165 Google reviews, and a lot of very clean yards. Maintenance · irrigation · installs · HOA (480) 336-2926 #MesaAZ #GilbertAZ #Landscaping #EastValley

Website article

Is your sprinkler bill too high? Check these 4 things 1. A head that sprays the sidewalk wastes water every cycle. Adjust or replace it. 2. Puddles or soggy spots usually mean a leak in the line, not too much watering. 3. A valve that won’t shut off isn’t always broken: roots can crush lines and fittings. 4. Reset the timer each season. Summer schedules in winter waste the most water. Need a hand? Call Higher Ground at (480) 336-2926.
